problem: Estimate robot policy rankings without manually rebuilding a simulator or running every comparison on hardware.
contribution: WorldGym is a diffusion-forcing action-conditioned video environment with variable prediction horizons matched to policy chunks and a VLM outcome judge. It is explicitly a proxy whose agreement must be established on actual paired trials.
algorithm: Latent DiT uses causal temporal attention, per-frame linear action embeddings in timestep/AdaLN conditioning, clipwise action dropout and classifier-free action guidance. Initialize from real first frame, alternate policy chunks with generated next frames and estimate success via MonteCarlo rollouts plus GPT4o. Optional partial-credit criteria differ from binary completion.
observations: Image history and low-level action chunks; task instruction for policy/reward. Prior OXE observation/action conventions and camera distributions determine coverage. No direct force/contact state is measured by video simulation.
actions: Variable-length policy chunks with one future frame per action; action embedding must retain each source embodiment's conventions. Supporting known morphologies does not establish calibrated unseen-arm transfer.
embodiment_and_data: OXE trajectories include Bridge,RT1,VIOLA,BerkeleyUR5. Main paired policy evaluation reuses recorded initial frames from17OpenVLA Bridge tasks,10trials/task/policy forRT1X,Octo,OpenVLA. Edited-image and altered-language tests create model-onlyOOD evaluations.
experiments: Replay held-out action sequences, single-action-dimension sweeps, real-versus-modeled policy success, known-version/checkpoint rankings and OODdistractors. Rankings by training-step/validationloss are indirect evidence; edited OOD estimates lack matched physical validation in main experiments.
baselines: RT1X,Octo,OpenVLA,earlier/smaller variants; video UniPi and diffusion DexVLA checkpoints. These compare evaluator consistency, not policy training gains. Real-world reference trials are reused from another study, not newly executed by this review.
quantitative_result: Figure4 PDFp5-6 Pearson per-task success correlationr0.78,p<.001. Real/model means RT1X18.5/15.6%,Octo20.0/23.8%,OpenVLA70.6/67.4%; claimed average absolute discrepancy~3.3percentagepoints. Figure13p9 edited-distractor model-onlyOpenVLA67.4→39.4%; this is not observed physical degradation.
limitations: Correlation and mean rank agreement do not calibrate every task or certify physical safety. Learned visual reward and video dynamics can share hallucination errors; known ranking confirmation may be weak on novel failures. OOD and force-sensitive interactions remain unsupported without real data. Conclusion acknowledges not all emulated interactions are realistic.
code_and_license: Independent code/model/OXE license audit not performed;GPT4o image use and source camera data require separate consideration. No code inspected/executed.
hardware_adaptation: ADAPT paired evaluation reports with actual versus model counts, correlations, absolute errors and failure-mode coverage. Use modeled rollouts for prioritization only until actualSO101/ROSMASTERcalibration and paired tests exist; generated frames cannot replace camera evidence for physical authorization or receiver hold.
